transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. How can I help you today?

Well, my lieutenant actually sent me here. I work as an EMT, and at the station... I was organizing the airway bags. I kept moving them into this pattern that I just knew was right, and I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud while I did it. 

My lieutenant came over and told me to stop and step away, but I wouldn't. I couldn't do it, because it felt like the whole bay would go bad if I broke the sequence. So, they told me I had to come see you.

Can you tell me more about what you were thinking while you were organizing the airway bags and repeating the dispatch numbers? Did certain thoughts keep coming into your mind that made you feel like you had to do things a certain way?

Well, I had to do it that way because... I know I'm being watched. The injury review people and some of the supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras. 

I was repeating the numbers and doing the pattern so there was proof I was doing things exactly right. Because they've been going into the system and changing my triage notes. They're trying to make me look unsafe on the job. I've brought it up to them, and they tell me it's just routine paperwork, but I know they're the ones changing my reports. So I couldn't break the sequence with the bags, or they would just use it against me.
Do you believe that the people watching you or altering your reports are part of a larger group or organization that's specifically targeting you?

Well, it's the injury review people and some of the supervisors. I don't know about some massive organization, but I know it's them. Like I said, they're watching me on the station cameras. And they're going into the computer and changing my triage notes. They want to make me look like I'm unsafe on the job, like I'm making mistakes. I've asked them about it, and they just brush it off, saying it's routine paperwork or quality assurance. But I know what I wrote, and I know they're the ones changing it. That's why I have to be so careful and do everything perfectly.
Have you ever found yourself speaking in a way that others have trouble following, or been told that your thoughts or speech were disorganized or didn't make sense?

No, I haven't been told that. People understand me fine. I mean, I have to speak clearly on the radio for dispatch every day, so my speech definitely makes sense. If anyone has trouble following what I'm saying, it's just because they don't want to admit what's actually going on with the cameras and the reports. But my thoughts are perfectly clear.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are not your own or that someone is putting thoughts into your head?

No, I don't... I don't feel like that at all. My thoughts are my own. Nobody is putting anything in my head. The problem isn't in my head, it's what they're doing on the computers and the cameras. I know what I'm thinking and I know what I'm seeing.
Have you ever had any beliefs or experiences that others might find strange or hard to believe, such as thinking that someone is controlling your actions or that you have special powers?

No, definitely not. I don't have any special powers or anything crazy like that. And nobody is controlling my actions. I'm in control of what I do. It's just... like I said, it's the supervisors and the review board messing with my reports and watching me. That's real, that's actually happening. But nobody is controlling my body or my mind.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being taken out of your head, put into your head, or broadcast out loud for others to hear?

No, I... I think I just said nobody is putting thoughts in my head. And no, they aren't taking them out either. Nobody can hear what I'm thinking out loud. My thoughts stay right here in my own head. They don't need to read my mind or broadcast anything anyway, because they're already watching me on the cameras and messing with my dispatch logs. So no, nothing like that is happening with my thoughts.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions outside of work that others might find unusual, like someone trying to harm you or a special role you believe you have?

No, not really. Outside of work, things are pretty normal. I don't think anyone is trying to harm me, and I definitely don't have any kind of special role or mission or anything like that. I just go home, try to relax, and mind my own business. The issues I'm having are just at work, with the supervisors and the dispatch system. Once I leave the station, I'm just a regular guy.

Do you believe, without any doubt, that the supervisors and injury review people are intentionally and deliberately altering your triage notes and watching you through cameras to make you look unsafe at work?

Yes. There is no doubt in my mind at all. I know for a fact that the injury review people and some of the supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras. And they are definitely going in and changing my triage notes to make me look unsafe on my calls. Whenever I try to say something about it, they just tell me it's routine paperwork or standard audits, but... I know exactly what they are actually doing.

Have you ever experienced any similar concerns or beliefs about people trying to harm you or alter your work in other settings, like in your personal life or other jobs, or is this limited to your current workplace?

No, it's just at this job. Like I said before, outside of work, things are fine. I've never had this happen at any other job I've worked at, either. It's just here, with these specific supervisors and the dispatch system they use. Nobody else is doing this to me.
Have you ever had any experiences or beliefs like this in other areas of your life, or is it strictly limited to what you're experiencing at work?

I think I just answered that, but... no, it's strictly limited to work. Like I just said, I don't have this going on anywhere else in my life. It's never happened at any other job, and my personal life is completely normal. It is just happening right now at the station.

Have you ever considered that there might be another explanation for the changes in your triage notes or the way your supervisors are acting, or do you believe there's no other possible explanation besides them deliberately targeting you?

No, there's no other explanation. I mean... I know what I see. I know the injury review people and some of the supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras. And I know they are changing my triage notes to make me look unsafe. They tell me it's just routine paperwork or standard audits, but that's just an excuse. I know what they're actually doing.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like someone is watching you or changing things in your life without your permission?

Doc, I... I feel like you keep asking me the exact same thing. No. Like I said a minute ago, outside of work, I don't feel that way at all. Nobody is watching me at my house or messing with my personal life. When I go home, everything is completely normal. It is only happening at the station.
Even though your supervisors have told you that the changes to your triage notes are routine, do you believe that they are lying to you or covering up their true intentions?
Yes, absolutely. I mean... I know they're lying. Like I just said, they call it routine paperwork, but that's just a cover-up. They are definitely lying to me about what they're really doing.

Even though there may be no objective evidence that your supervisors are altering your triage notes or watching you with the intent to harm you, do you still hold these beliefs with absolute certainty?

Yes, I'm absolutely certain. I know what's happening. I don't need... objective evidence when I'm living it. I know for a fact that the injury review people and the supervisors are watching me on those station cameras. And I know they are going in and changing my triage notes to make me look like I'm practicing unsafely. They can tell me all day that it's just routine paperwork, but I know the truth.
